turns.text: Turn back to 1768—1774: The Jaquet-Droz Automata begins with “The writing, drawing and music-making automata c” and asks us to rethink the relationship between machines, minds, and people.

The writing, drawing and music-making automata connected precision mechanics with lifelike action and audience fantasies of artificial life. They are important examples of automata before the modern idea of a robot. The work or idea appeared as technology, industrialization or modernity was reshaping cultural imagination.
The detail listeners may miss is “The Jaquet-Droz Automata”. Why does it become central to The Jaquet-Droz Automata?
It turns artificial making, autonomous action or computational decision into a discussion of agency, responsibility and social order.

Researchers generally treat this work as a cultural reference in AI humanities rather than a direct prediction of modern technology. It helped later publics discuss machines, labor, emotion and governance.
Next comes Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, where we will follow how “The Jaquet-Droz Automata” enters a new historical setting.
